subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value: MWCC GC 1.2.5 family. THIS SUPPLIES THE MISSING SOURCE SPELLING FOR THE FORWARD HALF OF claim.law.empty-block-branch-pair-splits-forward-vs-backedge.20260831.v1, AND BOUNDS IT. That law proved the forward `bCOND <next>` + `b <far>` pair is source-reachable and should be worked, but its two positive controls are both single-condition guards, so it never said what to write when the site has TWO guards. THE RULE: when the target shows the UNFUSED forward pair at the LAST test before a block, and your source spells that region as two consecutive early-out guards `if (A) EXIT; if (B) EXIT;`, MERGE THEM INTO ONE GUARD `if (A || B) EXIT;`. MWCC lowers two separate guards by short-circuiting each independently to the exit, which fuses the final test into a single inverted conditional (`beq <exit>`); it lowers ONE disjunctive guard by branching the final disjunct's FALSE edge AROUND to the block (`bne <block>`) and leaving the TRUE edge as a bare `b <exit>` - which IS the unfused pair. Measured on fn_8004DB3C: `if (delta > 0 && alpha >= 255) return; if (delta < 0 && alpha == 0) return;` fused (T60/O59, one instruction short, real 19); `if ((delta > 0 && alpha >= 255) || (delta < 0 && alpha == 0)) return;` produced the pair and the function went BYTE-EXACT in that single probe. THE DIAGNOSTIC TELL, which is what makes this cheap to spot: inside one function, guard 1 fuses in target (`bge <exit>`) while guard 2 does NOT. Two guards written as two statements lower identically to each other; an asymmetry between them means the target's source did not have two statements there. Look for the asymmetry before spelling anything. THE BOUNDARY, measured the same day on damage_enemy in the same TU and the reason this record is not a blanket lever: THE EXIT MUST BE THE FUNCTION EPILOGUE (a `return`), NOT AN INTERIOR MERGE POINT. damage_enemy's residual at 0x5ac is the identical forward pair, its guards are the identical `A && B` shape, and merging them changed nothing: both `if (!(health > upper || type == E_DEATH)) { block }` and `if (health > upper || type == E_DEATH) goto store_fight;` with the block following produced byte-identical output - the pair still folded to `beq`, at T571/O570 and real 151 versus the baseline's parity-exact 571/571 real 66. So the lever is not about the disjunction per se: it works because a `return` transfers to a block (the epilogue) the front end has ALREADY materialised for other reasons, satisfying the parent law's own condition that the target block be 'genuinely reached from elsewhere too'. A `goto` to an interior label does not satisfy it, because that label exists only for this guard. SCREEN BEFORE SPENDING A PROBE: merged-disjunction is worth one probe when the guard body is `return`; when the body is a jump to an interior merge point, the site is governed by attempt.parked.damage-enemy-p6-goto-pair.20260831.v1's do-not-retry list instead and should not be re-spelled. SECOND-ORDER NOTE, also measured: a comparison written to be negated (`health <= upper` used as a skip condition) lowers through `cror eq,lt,eq` + `bne` because that form is unordered-safe, whereas the target's plain `bgt` is the positive `>` spelling; the two differ on NaN, so an ours-only `cror` next to a target-only `bgt` is direct evidence that the target's source wrote the POSITIVE comparison and therefore an early-out, independent of any branch-fusion question.
